public_rationale: TIME published its report on 2023-01-18. It says OpenAI began sending tens of thousands of text snippets to an outsourcing firm in Kenya in November 2021. Some of those snippets described child sexual abuse and bestiality in graphic detail (e2). TIME reviewed internal documents and payslips and interviewed four workers. It reports that Sama labellers on the OpenAI project took home about $1.32 to $2 per hour, depending on seniority and performance (e1). Most of the labellers were junior agents. Citing three Sama employees, TIME says agents took home $1.32 to $1.44 per hour, and senior quality analysts up to $2 (e3). An OpenAI spokesperson told TIME that Sama employees in Kenya contributed to a toxic-content detection tool that was later built into ChatGPT (e1). A Sama spokesperson said workers could earn $1.46 to $3.74 per hour after taxes but declined to say which roles earned the higher rates (e3). The reported pay and tasks match the claim that a bunch of the work was done for under $2 per hour.
limitations: All the evidence comes from one investigative report, TIME's article of 2023-01-18. No independent source in the packet confirms the pay figures or the content of the tasks.

OpenAI's statement to TIME confirmed only that Sama workers in Kenya contributed to a toxic-content detector later built into ChatGPT. It did not confirm the pay rates or the specific material labelled.
Senior quality analysts could take home up to $2 per hour, which is not strictly less than $2.
Sama gave a higher pay range of $1.46 to $3.74 per hour without breaking it down by role, so it cannot be fully reconciled with TIME's figures.
The evidence does not show what share of all of ChatGPT's human filtering work Sama's Kenyan workers did. TIME says it is unclear whether OpenAI used other labelling firms for this project.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: A bunch of the human filtering work behind ChatGPT was done by poorly paid workers in Kenya, paid less than $2/hour to evaluate graphic material such as descriptions of sexual situations involving children and animals.

statement.excerpt: A bunch of that work was done poorly paid labor in Kenya, paid less than $2/hour to evaluate (e.g.) graphic descriptions of sexual situations involving children and animals that I prefer not to describe it in detail.

from_speaker: to evaluate (e.g.) graphic descriptions of sexual situations involving children and animals
our_interpretation: Plain reading: a meaningful part of the human filtering work for ChatGPT was done by Kenyan workers who took home under about $2 per hour and labelled graphic text, including child sexual abuse and bestiality.
Period: the Sama text-labelling contract for OpenAI, from November 2021 to March 2022.
'Less than $2/hour' is read as take-home pay up to about $2, matching the TIME headline he cites.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable reporting shows Kenyan contractors labelled graphic sexual content involving children and animals for OpenAI's ChatGPT safety work, for take-home pay of about $2/hour or less.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence shows the workers were paid well above $2/hour, did not label such material, or that the work was unrelated to ChatGPT.
